study.title: Cerebral blood flow and functional connectivity immediate changes following intradermal acupuncture in major depressive disorder
study.study_design: Single-center neuroimaging substudy embedded within a multicenter randomized controlled trial; within-subject pre-post design for MDD patients; healthy controls scanned once for group comparison
study.randomization: Not reported for the neuroimaging substudy; parent trial was a randomized controlled trial
study.blinding: Not reported for the neuroimaging substudy
study.population: Twenty patients diagnosed with MDD and twenty age- and sex-matched healthy controls; all right-handed
study.inclusion_criteria: MDD diagnosis established by two senior psychiatrists using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5; HAMD-17 total score greater than 17 for MDD group; healthy controls screened using non-patient edition of the SCID to confirm absence of any current or past psychiatric disorders; all participants right-handed
study.exclusion_criteria: Contraindications to MRI; major psychotic disorders (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or other psychotic disorders); substance-related disorders; severe or unstable medical illnesses; positive suicidal tendency; pregnancy or lactation; inability to cooperate with study procedures; allergy to adhesive tape or fear of intradermal acupuncture; prior intradermal acupuncture treatment; participation in other clinical trials; for healthy controls: any personal history of psychiatric disorders or a first-degree family history of psychotic disorders

conditions.scan_context: Resting-state MRI (BOLD-fMRI and ASL) acquired before IA; participants instructed to lie flat and relaxed, keep eyes closed but stay awake

conditions.timepoint_exact: Immediately after intradermal acupuncture stimulation (after 8 min continuous IA stimulation and 5 min rest)
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state MRI (BOLD-fMRI and ASL) acquired immediately after IA; participants instructed to lie flat and relaxed, keep eyes closed but stay awake
Resting-state MRI (BOLD-fMRI and ASL) acquired once; no acupuncture

interventions.stimulation_type: Intradermal needling with manual pressing stimulation
interventions.laterality_exact: Bilateral; stimulated in the following order: left PC6, right PC6, left HT7, right HT7, left SP6, right SP6, left LR3, right LR3
interventions.manipulation_exact: Manual pressing stimulation applied for 1 min on each side at an approximate rhythm of 60 presses per minute; each acupoint received 2 min of stimulation in total
interventions.session_duration_exact: 8 min of continuous IA stimulation (total across all 8 acupoint sides)
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: Single session (one session before the second MRI scan)
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Lie flat and relaxed, keep eyes closed but stay awake
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Selection of acupoints (PC6, HT7, SP6, and LR3) was based on a previous data mining study on acupuncture treatment for MDD, which identified these acupoints as commonly used and clinically relevant for emotional regulation

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 3.0-Tesla General Electric scanners (Discovery MR750, GE Healthcare) equipped with an 8-channel head coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T1-weighted sagittal structural images, BOLD-fMRI images, cross-sectional T2-weighted images, ASL images, and CBF images automatically generated from the ASL images
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: Normalized CBF maps resampled to an isotropic voxel size of 3 mm
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: SPM12 (for CBF spatial normalization); BRANT toolbox (for FCS analysis); SPM8 (for GLM of zCBF/FCS ratio)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: 6 mm × 6 mm × 6 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel (for CBF); 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel (for FCS)
statistical_thresholds_exact: Intergroup comparisons of zCBF/FCS ratio: whole-brain voxel-wise independent t-test, GRF correction (voxel level p < 0.001 and cluster level p < 0.05)
Differences of zCBF and zFCS between two groups: independent t-tests, GRF correction (voxel level p < 0.005 and cluster level p < 0.05)
Paired differences in CBF/FCS ratio before and after IA: FDR corrected, voxel level p < 0.05 and cluster level p < 0.05
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: GRF correction (for intergroup comparisons); FDR correction (for pre-post paired comparison)

extraction_notes.note: Sensory/deqi responses were not assessed or reported. No deqi measurement instrument was mentioned in the methods or results.
No sham acupuncture control group was included. The authors acknowledge this as a major limitation; effects cannot be attributed specifically to intradermal acupuncture.
Expectancy and blinding assessments were not performed or reported. Authors note this limitation implicitly in the discussion.
Adverse events are not reported in the paper.

Supplementary Table 1 (detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria) and Supplementary Figure 1 (HC vs. MDD group comparison of CBF/FCS) and detailed scanning parameters and preprocessing (Supplementary material) are referenced but not provided in the main PDF. Coordinate data for the HC vs. MDD group comparison are not available from the main text or table.

Detailed MRI acquisition parameters (TR, TE, flip angle, slice thickness, number of volumes, scan duration for BOLD and ASL) are stated to be in Supplementary material and were not extracted due to absence of supplementary data in the provided PDF.

The 'statistic type' for Table 2 cluster results is labelled 'Peak intensity' in the table header; it is unclear whether this represents a t-statistic, F-statistic, or another metric. Preserved exactly as reported.

The MNI coordinate for cluster 8 (Precuneus_R: 24, 63, 51) has a very high positive y-value (63), which may represent an anterior location unusual for precuneus. This coordinate is extracted verbatim as reported in Table 2 without correction.

The paper reports the HC vs. MDD CBF/FCS group comparison results in Supplementary Figure 1 only; no coordinate table is provided in the main text for this comparison. The result_level for this contrast is set to 'figure_only'.

The study design is described as a neuroimaging substudy of a multicenter RCT; however, the neuroimaging substudy itself did not include a randomized sham control or parallel group for MDD patients. The pre-post design for MDD patients means that neural change results cannot be causally attributed to acupuncture specifically.

The paper describes Figure 4 as showing 'paired differences in CBF/FCS ratio before and after IA (FDR corrected, voxel level p < 0.05 and cluster level p < 0.05)' but the methods section for intergroup comparison uses GRF correction at voxel level p < 0.001. The pre-post analysis uses FDR correction at a less stringent threshold. These are two different analyses with different correction methods, extracted separately.
No information on medication status (whether MDD patients were on antidepressants at time of scanning) is reported in the main text.
